text:
Sam: FYI seeing a sustained burst from tenant-42 in us-east-1 — they're consuming ~70% of the shared-GPU queue for the last 20m, p95 queue wait up 3x.
Maya: Oof. Is this a single job type or many small requests?
Sam: Mostly short-chat generation, high qps spikes. Not long-running.
Jorge: Sounds like classic noisy-tenant. Current per-tenant rate caps are static and too coarse.
Li: Can we try a smoothing/adaptive limiter instead of hard throttle? e.g., per-tenant leaky bucket whose leak rate adapts to cluster free capacity.
Sam: That's what I was sketching — "burst-dampener": allow short bursts but scale down sustained rate based on available tokens in the shared pool.
Tariq: Important: we need graceful degradation for latency-sensitive SLAs. Hard drops would regress customers.
Maya: Agree. Proposal: token-bucket per-tenant with three levers: base_rate (fair share), burst_allowance (short-term), and a dynamic multiplier = min(1, available_pool_tokens / pool_threshold).
Jorge: Also add a soft-park path: if tenant stays above sustained multiplier for N minutes, move them to a parked queue with lower CPU/GPU affinity and a slower leak rate. Not full eviction, just slower.
Sam: Parked queue + queued retry header so SDKs can surface backpressure.
Li: Example config I prototyped:
```yaml
admission_control:
  per_tenant:
    enabled: true
    base_rate_tokens_per_sec: 10
    burst_capacity_tokens: 50
    park_after_minutes: 5
    dynamic_multiplier_threshold: 0.15 # fraction of pool tokens
```
Jorge: Nice. How to compute pool tokens? sum of all node free slots weighted by model memory footprint?
Sam: We can use the runtime's KV cache sizing + free_kernel_slots metric to derive an "effective capacity" number. Keep it coarse to avoid flapping.
Tariq: What metrics do we expose so SRE can monitor impact?
Maya: Need p95/p99 intraday queue_wait, park_count by tenant, burst_triggers, and token_drain_rate. Also SLA erroring calls and retry-after headers.
infra-bot: Alert: high_queue_wait detected in us-east-1 at 2026-11-03T14:06:01Z (rule: queue_wait_p95>500ms).
Sam: Plan for rollout: start in canary region (us-west-2) on shared pool B, 1% tenants opt-in via feature-flag, monitor park_count and p99 latency for 48h.
Li: For fairness, initialize base_rate using small-sample fairshare: base_rate = max(1, floor(total_capacity / active_tenants)). Then adjust every 5m.
Jorge: Edge case: multi-tenant jobs that fanout across tens of shards could accumulate tokens fast. We should have a per-workload aggregation key to avoid compound bursts.
Maya: Good call. Also expose an override for enterprise Dedicated customers (don't park them on shared pools).
Tariq: Cost angle: parking reduces GPU utilization but prevents noisy tenants from increasing overall tail latency — tradeoff is marginal from our current billing mix. We'll capture utilization delta in the canary.
Sam: Backpressure semantics for SDKs: return 429 with Retry-After for transient park; return 503 only on system-level capacity out. Prefer 429 + Retry-After.
Li: Implementation notes: admission layer sits right before routing; dynamic multiplier computed from sliding 30s window; smoothing with EMA alpha=0.2 to avoid oscillation.
Jorge: Any thought on using priority lanes? low-prio lane gets best-effort batching but longer cold-start.
Maya: Yes, priority lanes + park is cleaner than eviction. Low priority can be scheduled on lower-cost nodes.
Sam: Action items: 
- Li: add prototype limiter and config to staging (ETA 2d)
- Jorge: instrument park_count, token_drain_rate dashboards (ETA 3d)
- Maya: prepare canary selection criteria and rollout playbook (ETA 1d)
- Tariq: cost impact analysis for parked workloads (ETA 4d)
Jorge: I'll also add an alert if park_count exceeds 5% of active tenants in region.
Sam: Cool. If everyone agrees I'll flip a PR tomorrow. Keep chatter short as we test. :thumbsup:
Maya: SGTM.
Li: On it.
Tariq: Thanks.
infra-bot: Deployment job queued: roll/admission-proto -> staging (build 2026.11.03-847).
